The [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]] competed in the [[Pac-12 Conference]] and were led by head coach [[Ben Howland]]. Prior to the start of the season, the Bruins took a Goodwill Tour of [[China]] in late August. The Bruins reopened the newly renovated [[Pauley Pavilion]] on November 9, 2012 in front of a then record crowd of 13,513. On March 9, 2013, the Bruins clinched the regular season championship of the Pac-12 Conference by defeating [[2012–13 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]], 61–54, to finish conference play with a record of 13–5. They were seeded as the No. 1 team in the [[2013 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 Conference tournament]] in [[Las Vegas Valley|Las Vegas]]. They were defeated by Oregon in the championship game. A week later, the Bruins were eliminated in the second round of the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2013 NCAA tournament]] by Minnesota 83–63 to finish the season 25–10. After the season, on March 25, 2013, coach [[Ben Howland]] was fired by UCLA.{{cite news |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/college/basketball/la-sp-plaschke-ben-howland-20130325,0,7489477.column UCLA.JPG|thumb|150px|Shabazz Muhammad at [[Pauley Pavilion]] in December 2012]] Before the season's opening game, freshman [[Shabazz Muhammad]] was declared ineligible to participate by the NCAA.{{cite news|last=Yoon |first=Peter |title=Shabazz Muhammad ineligible |date=November 9, 2012 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/ncb/story/_/id/8612665/shabazz-muhammad-ruled-ineligible-ucla-bruins |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121111061416/http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/ncb/story/_/id/8612665/shabazz-muhammad-ruled-ineligible-ucla-bruins |archive-date=November 11, 2012 |url-status=live }} He was ruled to have received improper benefits for travel expenses and lodging during unofficial visits to Duke and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]. After missing three games and an appeal by UCLA, he was reinstated, and his family was required to repay approximately $1,600.{{cite news|last=Yoon |first=Peter |title=Shabazz Muhammad eligible to play |date=November 16, 2012 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/ncb/story/_/id/8640531/shabazz-muhammad-ucla-bruins-reinstated-ncaa |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121117192601/http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/ncb/story/_/id/8640531/shabazz-muhammad-ucla-bruins-reinstated-ncaa |archive-date=November 17, 2012 |url-status=live }} He scored 15 points off the bench in his debut in a 78–70 loss to [[2012–13 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] in the semifinals of the [[Legends Classic (basketball tournament)|Legends Classic]]. [[Jordan Adams (basketball, born 1994)|Jordan Adams]] added 22 points in the game, extending his school record to four games of 20-point games by a freshman to start a season.{{cite news|last=Spector|first=Jesse|title=UCLA vs. Georgetown: Shabazz Muhammad's debut ends in defeat|date=November 19, 2012|work=sportingnews.com|url=http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2012-11-19/ucla-bruins-vs-georgetown-hoyas-score-shabazz-muhammad-debut-jordan-adams-stats|access-date=November 20, 2012|archive-date=February 3, 2013|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130203134524/http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2012-11-19/ucla-bruins-vs-georgetown-hoyas-score-shabazz-muhammad-debut-jordan-adams-stats|url-status=dead}}{{cite news |last=Holmes |first=Baxter |title=Shabazz Muhammad shows he's a quick study as UCLA beats Georgia |date=November 21, 2012 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/college/basketball/la-sp-1121-ucla-georgia-20121121,0,1189838.story |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121121130359/http://www.latimes.com/sports/college/basketball/la-sp-1121-ucla-georgia-20121121,0,1189838.story |archive-date=2012-11-21 |url-status=live |access-date=2012-11-21 }} Muhammad became a starter in the next game against [[2012–13 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]], and he scored a game-high 21 points in a 60–56 win in the Classic's consolation game. The following game, UCLA led [[2012–13 Cal Poly Mustangs men's basketball team|Cal Poly]] by 18 points with 12 minutes remaining before they were upset, 70–68. Earlier in the year, the Bruins needed overtime to defeat another [[Big West]] team, [[2012–13 UC Irvine Anteaters men's basketball team|UC Irvine]].{{cite news|last=Brennan |first=Eamonn |title=Poll Thoughts: See you, UCLA |date=November 26, 2012 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/68274/poll-thoughts-see-you-ucla |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121129103232/http://espn.go.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/68274/poll-thoughts-see-you-ucla |archive-date=November 29, 2012 |url-status=live }} UCLA dropped out of the [[AP Poll]] after being ranked No. 11.{{cite news|title=UCLA coughs up 18-point lead in stunning loss to Cal Poly |date=November 25, 2012 |work=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=323300026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121129101330/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=323300026 |archive-date=November 29, 2012 |url-status=dead }} UCLA lost 78–69 in the [[John R. Wooden Classic]] to the [[2012–13 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State Aztecs]], the Bruins' first ranked opponent of the year. Although it was a neutral-site game in nearby [[Anaheim]], the crowd favored the Aztecs.{{cite news |last=Holmes |first=Baxter |title=Bruins fall to Aztecs, 78-69, at John R. Wooden Classic |date=December 2, 2012 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/college/basketball/la-sp-1202-ucla-basketball-20121202,0,9040.story |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121204013155/http://www.latimes.com/sports/college/basketball/la-sp-1202-ucla-basketball-20121202,0,9040.story |archive-date=2012-12-04 |url-status=live |access-date=2012-12-03 }} UCLA won its next 10 games, including an upset win over #7 Missouri, before losing to No. 16 [[2012–13 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]]. It followed with an 84–73 road win over No. 6 [[2012–13 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] behind Muhammad's game-high 23 points.{{cite news|title=UCLA rides huge start to surprise No. 6 Arizona |date=January 24, 2013 |work=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330240012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130125075240/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330240012 |archive-date=January 25, 2013 |url-status=live }} After losing their next two games, to [[2012–13 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]] and [[2012–13 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]], the Bruins won seven of their final nine games, clinching the regular season [[2012-13 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12]] title in their final regular season game, with a win over [[2012–13 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] in [[Seattle]] on March 9. During the game, [[point guard]] [[Larry Drew II]] broke [[Pooh Richardson]]'s school record for single-season assists.{{cite news|last=Loumena|first=Dan|title=UCLA clinches Pac-12 Conference regular-season title|date=March 9, 2013|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/sportsnow/la-sp-ucla-washington-recap-20130309,0,4683106.story|access-date=March 10, 2013}}
